newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares advance in early bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares advance in early bourse trade.

text.p: German shares defied forecasts of a lower start to the week and strengthened in early bourse trade on Monday, as traders incorporated the possible effect of a rise in U.S. interest rates into their trading strategies.
Early on, the DAX index of 30 blue-chip shares stood at 3,321.52 points, up 23.28 points or 0.71 percent, while the June DAX future was up 3,331 points, up 26 points.
"The market is suprisingly strong this morning. The main factor is that the market has factored in a 25-basis point hike in U.S. interest rates," said a Frankfurt trader.

Speculation of a possible interest rate hike intensified last week after comments by the chairman of the U.S. Federal Reserve, Alan Greenspan, which were interpreted by market players as pointing towards a rise in key rates.

As bourse trade in Frankfurt opened, focus was on Thyssen AG, which was up 25.50 marks, or 6.52 pct at 416.50 marks, rising on reports it was planning to tell shareholders its shares have the potential to reach a price of around 550 marks.
Last week Krupp-Hoesch announced a takeover bid. Since then Thyssen agreed to discuss a joint steel company. If the talks fail, Krupp said it planned to reinstate the offer.
Krupp also benefited from the reports, and rose 10 marks, or 3.15 percent, to 327 marks in bourse trade.

Other corporate news in early trade included a repeat of an earlier denial by Deutsche Bank AG that it had an agreement to "pool" its 25.8 percent in builder Philipp Holzmann AG with a stake held by Hochtief AG.
Holzmann shares were unchanged from their closing price on Friday of 520 marks, while Hochtief shares were up 1.30 marks, nearly two percent, at 71.50 marks.
